facts.text: East Los Angeles was originally called East Los Angeles when founded in 1873, but residents voted to rename it Lincoln Heights in 1917.
The East Los Angeles Library opened on May 1, 1923 as a modest book collection in a storefront before moving to its current location in 1972.
Adjacent to the library is a Japanese library and dojo that helped popularize judo, turning the area into a cultural hub for martial arts.
Brooklyn Avenue, now known as Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, has long been the heart of East Los Angeles, hosting early labor union offices and community shops.
Belvedere Community Regional Park, built in 1942 as Soledad Park, now offers an Olympic‑size pool, skate park, and splash pad for residents.
